rules.title: Never type `!`
rules.statement: `!` is a type (the never type), parsed as a type reference named `!`.

rules.title: Unit type `()`
rules.statement: `()` denotes the unit type, the empty tuple type.

rules.title: Tuple type
rules.statement: A tuple type is `(T1, T2, ...)` with ≥2 comma-separated element types (optional trailing comma), or a 1-element tuple `(T,)` requiring the trailing comma.

rules.title: Variadic-arity tuple target `(A...)`
rules.statement: `(A...)` is a variadic-arity tuple type naming pack-typevar A; used as an impl target `impl<A...> Trait for (A...)`. Resolves to a Tuple type with one variadic element naming A.
rules.divergence: Logos addition: variadic tuple impls (no direct Rust equivalent).

rules.title: Raw fat-pointer to slice
rules.statement: `*const [T]` and `*mut [T]` are raw fat pointers to a slice, sharing the `{*const T, usize}` ABI of `&[T]` but without borrow-check guarantees. These alternatives precede plain pointer/array forms so the bare `[T]` parses.

rules.title: Raw pointer type
rules.statement: `*const T` is an immutable raw pointer and `*mut T` is a mutable raw pointer to T.

rules.title: Zoned raw pointer `*zoned [mut] T`
rules.statement: `*zoned T` / `*zoned mut T` is a zoned raw pointer (Ref-arm self-relative at rest; deref/assign runs the storage↔compute bridge). `zoned` is a contextual keyword recognized only in pointer position (a bare IDENT after `*`), validated as NAME=="zoned" by sema; it is not globally reserved.
rules.divergence: Logos addition (F3 ref-repr design): zoned pointers, no Rust equivalent.

rules.title: Fixed-size array type `[T; N]`
rules.statement: `[T; N]` is a fixed-size array type where N is an integer literal or an identifier (const generic). Size-bearing forms are matched before the unsized fallback.

rules.title: Array size from variadic pack length
rules.statement: `[T; P...(P)]` sizes the array from a variadic pack length; lowered to symbolic array-size-var `__sizeof_pack:P` and resolved at monomorphization.

rules.title: Array size from metacall
rules.statement: `[T; metacall { ... }]` permits a compile-time metacall block as the array size expression.
rules.divergence: Logos: comptime sizing via explicit metacall (see explicit-metacall design).

rules.title: Unsized slice type `[T]`
rules.statement: Bare `[T]` (no size) is the unsized slice type. The size-bearing array forms are tried first, so `[T; N]` always wins over the unsized fallback.

rules.title: Generic type-argument kinds
rules.statement: A generic type argument may be a lifetime `'a` (stored as LIFETIME_PARAM and skipped during concrete-type resolution), a pack expansion `Ident...`, an antiquote `$Ident` or `$Ident...`, an integer literal (optionally negated), a writ literal, or a type.

rules.title: Fully-qualified non-generic type path
rules.statement: A fully-qualified non-generic type in type position is written `pkg.path.Type` (dotted); the last path segment is the type. Matched before bare-IDENT alternatives so the whole dotted form is claimed. The generic dotted form `pkg.path.Type<A>` is not supported (use a `use` import + short name).
rules.divergence: Logos path model: `.` for package/module path, `::` for items.

rules.title: Generic type instantiation `T<...>`
rules.statement: `Name<arg, ...>` (optional trailing comma) instantiates a generic type. The type name may also be a metavariable: `#Ident<...>` or `#(expr)<...>`.

rules.title: Metavariable type reference
rules.statement: `#Ident` and `#(expr)` are type references whose name is supplied by a metaprogram variable/expression rather than a literal identifier.

rules.title: Block
rules.statement: A block is `{ stmt* }`: a brace-delimited sequence of zero or more statements.

rules.title: Unsafe block
rules.statement: `unsafe { ... }` is an unsafe block whose body is an ordinary block.

rules.title: Nested function statement
rules.statement: A `fn name(params) [-> T] { ... }` at statement position is a nested function: its body is lifted to a top-level free function and the local name binds a fn-ptr value. A nested fn captures nothing; reads of enclosing locals are rejected (use a closure instead).

rules.title: Statement forms
rules.statement: A statement is one of: nested-fn, labeled-loop, let-else, let, for, while, loop, return, break, continue, deref-write, if-expr, match, destructure-assign, assign, compound-assign, place-assign, unsafe-block, block, `expr ;` (expression statement), or a trailing `expr` (block tail value). A block without a trailing `;` yields its final expression as the block value.

rules.title: For-range loop
rules.statement: `for i in lo..hi { }` iterates the exclusive integer range; `for i in lo..=hi { }` iterates the inclusive range.

rules.title: For-each loop
rules.statement: `for x in iter { }` iterates over an iterable. The loop variable may be a simple identifier (fast path) or a full destructuring pattern `for (a,b) in v { }`, in which case the pattern is bound against each element.

rules.title: loop block
rules.statement: `loop { ... }` is an unconditional loop.

rules.title: Labeled loop
rules.statement: `'label: for/while/loop { ... }` attaches a lifetime-syntax label to a loop, targetable by `break 'label` / `continue 'label`.

rules.title: break
rules.statement: `break;`, `break expr;`, `break 'label;`, and `break 'label expr;` are all valid; a value and/or a target label are optional. A bare `break` may also be terminated by `,`.

rules.title: continue
rules.statement: `continue;` and `continue 'label;` are valid; the target label is optional. A bare `continue` may also be terminated by `,`.

rules.title: Match statement
rules.statement: `match SCRUT { ARM* }` matches a scrutinee against arms. A bare-identifier scrutinee is parsed specially (as a var-ref) so `match e { ... }` does not mis-parse `e {` as a struct literal; complex scrutinee expressions fall through to the general expr form.

rules.title: Match arm with optional guard
rules.statement: A match arm is `PAT [if GUARD] => BODY`, where BODY is a block, an expression, or a statement, with an optional trailing comma. The optional `if GUARD` is a guard expression gating the arm.

rules.title: Let-binding tuple pattern
rules.statement: A let-binding tuple pattern admits `()` (unit), `..` rest (expanded to the right number of `_` skips), nested tuples `(a, (b, c))`, and identifier bindings. Rest fills remaining positions so names land on the correct tuple slots.

rules.title: Or-pattern
rules.statement: A pattern is one or more `pat_single` alternatives separated by `|`, with an optional leading `|`. A variant-payload arg may itself be an or-pattern `Some(A | B)`; a single alternative passes through transparently.

rules.title: Struct-pattern field
rules.statement: A struct-pattern field is `..` (rest), `name: subpat`, `0: subpat` (tuple-struct field by index, resolved positionally), `ref name`, `ref mut name`, or a bare `name` shorthand binding the field to a same-named local.

rules.title: Slice-pattern rest binding
rules.statement: A slice-pattern element may be `name @ ..` (binds the trailing/middle sub-slice to a name), `..` (anonymous rest), or a regular sub-pattern.

rules.title: Tuple-pattern rest element
rules.statement: A tuple-pattern element may be `..` (rest, converted to `_` wildcard skips preserving fixed arity) or an or-pattern of sub-patterns.

rules.title: At-binding pattern
rules.statement: `name @ subpat` binds `name` to the value matched by `subpat`. `ref name @ subpat` binds by reference.

rules.title: ref / ref mut / mut bindings
rules.statement: `ref x` binds the matched place by shared reference; `ref mut x` by mutable reference; `mut x` introduces a fresh mutable binding by value.

rules.title: Reference patterns
rules.statement: `&pat` and `&mut pat` match a reference, peeling one scrutinee reference layer. `&&pat` / `&&mut pat` (lexed as `AND`) peels two layers, producing nested reference patterns.

rules.title: Unit pattern `()`
rules.statement: `()` is the unit pattern, matching the unit value.

rules.title: Writ scalar patterns
rules.statement: `@null`, `@true`/`@false`, `@N`/`@-N`, and `@"str"` are writ scalar patterns matching writ null, bool, integer, and string values respectively.

rules.title: Writ typed map/array patterns
rules.statement: `@<T>{..}`, `@<T,R>{..}`, and `@<T>[..]` are typed writ map and array patterns annotating the matched container's element type(s).

rules.title: Writ map/array patterns
rules.statement: `@{ key: pat, ... }` / `@{}` match writ maps; `@[ elem, ... ]` / `@[]` match writ arrays. Array elements admit a trailing `..` to match length ≥ n; map keys are string literals.

rules.title: Enum tuple-variant pattern
rules.statement: `E::V(args)` matches an enum tuple-variant payload; payload args are full nested patterns, possibly including `..` rest and or-patterns. A bare `Foo(a, b)` (no `::`) matches a tuple-struct when the name resolves as a tuple-struct rather than an enum.

rules.title: Enum struct-variant pattern
rules.statement: `E::V { x, y: pat, .. }` / `E::V {}` match a struct-shaped enum variant; field names resolve to variant payload indices.

rules.title: Fieldless variant pattern
rules.statement: `E::V` matches a fieldless (unit) enum variant.

rules.title: Struct pattern
rules.statement: `Point { field_list }` / `Point {}` destructure a struct by named fields.

rules.title: Slice pattern
rules.statement: `[elems]` / `[]` match a slice/array by element patterns.

rules.title: Integer range patterns
rules.statement: Integer range patterns include closed inclusive `lo..=hi`, closed exclusive `lo..hi`, and half-open forms `a..` (RangeFrom → [a, TYPE_MAX]), `..=b` (RangeToInclusive → [TYPE_MIN, b]), `..b` (RangeToExclusive → [TYPE_MIN, b-1]). Each endpoint may be negated (`-N`). Open bounds clamp to the scrutinee type's min/max.

rules.title: Integer literal patterns
rules.statement: `N` matches an integer literal; `-N` matches a negative integer literal.

rules.title: Char patterns
rules.statement: `'a'` matches a char literal; `'a'..='z'` matches an inclusive char range.

rules.title: Float-literal pattern rejected
rules.statement: A float-literal pattern parses but is rejected by sema with a diagnostic: float equality matching in patterns is deliberately not supported (IEEE equality semantics undefined).
rules.divergence: Rust deprecated float patterns; Logos rejects them outright.

rules.title: Byte-string pattern rejected
rules.statement: A byte-string-literal pattern parses but is rejected by sema (pending &[u8] equality-matching codegen).
rules.uncertainty: Status is provisional ("until codegen lands"); reflects current compiler behavior.

rules.title: String-literal pattern
rules.statement: A string-literal pattern `"foo"` matches by string equality (lowered to a refutable `str_eq(scrut, "foo")` guard over a wildcard binding).

rules.title: Bool patterns
rules.statement: `true` and `false` match the boolean values.

rules.title: Parenthesised / grouped pattern
rules.statement: `(P)` is exactly P and `(P | Q | ...)` is a grouped or-pattern (inlined into a single or-pattern at that position). `(..)` matches any tuple binding nothing (irrefutable wildcard).

rules.title: Tuple pattern
rules.statement: `(a, b, ...)` is a tuple pattern (≥2 elements) admitting a `..` rest at any single position; `(x,)` (trailing comma) is a 1-tuple pattern, distinguished from a parenthesised pattern `(x)`.

rules.title: Identifier / wildcard pattern
rules.statement: A bare identifier is an irrefutable binding pattern (the matched value is bound to the name; `_` is the anonymous wildcard).

rules.title: let-else statement
rules.statement: `let PAT = expr else { block };` binds a refutable pattern; on match failure the else block runs (which must diverge).

rules.title: let bindings
rules.statement: `let` supports: tuple destructure `let (a,b) [: T] = e;`, `let ref x [: T] = e;` (sugar for `let x = &e;`), `let mut x [: T] [= e];` (mutable, type-only declaration without init allowed when typed), `let x [: T] [= e];`, and `let PAT = e;` (irrefutable full pattern, refutability checked by sema).

rules.title: while and while-let
rules.statement: `while cond { }` is a conditional loop; `while let PAT = e [&& guard] { }` is a while-let loop; `while LET-CHAIN { }` is a while-let chain (≥2 segments starting with let), ordered first so it is not shadowed.

rules.title: return statement
rules.statement: `return [expr];` returns from the enclosing function with an optional value; may be terminated by `;` or `,`.

rules.title: Simple variable assignment
rules.statement: `name = expr;` assigns to a simple variable place.

rules.title: General place assignment
rules.statement: `PLACE = expr;` where PLACE is an arbitrary postfix-chain lvalue (chained index `a[i][j]`, deref+tuple-index `(*p).0`, deeper mixes); sema computes the address and emits a deref-write. Tried after the specialized single/two-level write forms and after bare-variable assignment.

rules.title: Destructuring assignment into existing places
rules.statement: Tuple `(a, b) = e;`, array `[a, b] = e;`, and struct `S { f, .. } = e;` destructuring assignment writes into existing places (RFC 2909). Parsed before expr-statements so a parenthesised/bracketed LHS followed by `=` is recognized.

rules.title: Compound assignment over any place
rules.statement: `PLACE op= expr` applies a compound assignment over an arbitrary place: a bare variable takes the simple-var path; any other place desugars to `place = place op rhs` (or an `*Assign` trait-method call). Bare-deref `*p op= v` is handled separately (it is not an atom).
